extension.description: Reviews kindling's `kling` CLI (Firecracker/Virtualization.framework microVMs with a docker-style interface) and the `kling-db`, `kling-mcp` and `kling-phone` extension binaries: credential and secret handoff and database copies at the strictest tier, removal and rollback of machines, volumes, templates and databases, provisioning of new machines, MCP services and extensions, and everyday command execution inside an existing machine. Read-only commands (ps, logs, inspect, top, status, doctor, version, machine audit, graph audit, db audit, the ls/inspect subcommands) match no rule here; kling is not on Guard's built-in safe-command list, so the unknown-executable review floor still applies to them. No safe variants are offered: kling answers -h/--help anywhere before `--` without running the command, but an environment variable kling reads can switch that interception off and a declarative matcher cannot see the inherited environment.
extension.name: kindling microVM protection

permissions.description: Identifies commands that move a real secret into or out of a kindling microVM. `kling machine credential` and `kling template credential` hand an API key or a Postgres/MySQL password to kindling's credential proxy (read from a file or stdin, tied to one machine or to every machine later born from a template); `kling machine secret` (legacy `kling mmds`, `kling machine mmds`) injects a session secret through MMDS; `kling db connect -dsn` prints a database DSN that includes the password; `kling phone token` prints a phone API token. The guest never sees the key in the proxy case, but the agent running the command is the one choosing which key goes where, so every invocation needs a fresh human decision.
permissions.example_command: kling machine credential api -domain api.example.com -env API_KEY
permissions.label: kindling credential or secret handoff
safer_guidance: Have a person run the credential or secret command, or approve it each time, and scope it with -allow-request.
Prefer `kling db connect -psql` (password passed through the environment) over printing a DSN.

permissions.description: Identifies `kling db` commands that duplicate or share database contents: `db fork` (N live copies of a running copy, data included), `db branch` (a copy per git branch forked from its parent), `db clone` and `db slice` (read a production Postgres URL and dump it, masked, into a microVM), and `db attach` (gives an agent in another machine access to a copy through the proxy). The same subcommands are matched when the `kling-db` extension binary is invoked directly. `db branch -ls`/`-switch` also match: the matcher cannot tell the listing flags apart from a positional branch name reliably, and the unknown-executable review floor applies to them anyway.
permissions.label: kindling database copy or share
safer_guidance: Use `kling db up <template>` for a fresh copy from a template instead of forking one that holds live data.
Grant `kling db role <copy> -ro` read-only access instead of attaching a full copy to another agent.

permissions.description: Identifies commands that destroy or roll back kindling state: `kling rm` and `kling stop` (machine and its snapshot), `sandbox rm`, `graph rm`, `volume rm` and `volume restore` (overwrites the current volume, keeping only `<name>@undo`), `template rm` (legacy `rmi`, `snapshots rm`), `image rm`, `plugin rm`/`uninstall`, and in the extensions `db rm`, `db reset`, `db undo`, `db env down`, `db class rm|reset` and `phone rm`. The `remove` spellings and the plural nouns (`volumes`, `sandboxes`, `images`, `plugins`) are the aliases kling accepts. `-f` only skips kling's own confirmation prompt and is not needed for a match.
permissions.label: kindling resource removal or rollback
safer_guidance: Freeze instead of removing: `kling freeze <ref>` keeps the machine at zero RAM and it thaws in milliseconds.
Take `kling volume snapshot <name>` or `kling db snapshot <copy> <name>` before a restore, reset or removal.

permissions.description: Identifies commands that start new code or bring new code in: `kling run` and `kling try` (a microVM running an image, optionally with -egress internet and -share SRC:DST:rw, which mounts a host folder writable), `sandbox create`/`new` and `sandbox fork` (N copies of a live sandbox, memory and processes included), `graph up` and `graph fork`, `save` (legacy `commit`), `image build`, `image put`, `image copy`, `volume populate` (installs packages inside a microVM), `mcp add`, `mcp import`, `mcp migrate` and `mcp link` (host or link an MCP server that agents will call; legacy top-level `add` and `migrate`), and `plugin install` (downloads a kling extension binary). `-share ...:rw` is not matched separately because every command that accepts it is already covered here.
permissions.label: kindling machine, MCP service or extension provisioning
safer_guidance: Keep the default -egress none, or use -egress allowlist -allow <domains>, and prefer the default read-only -share copy mode.
Review the MCP server package or extension release before `kling mcp add` or `kling plugin install`.

permissions.description: Identifies `kling exec`, `kling shell` and `kling cp`, which run a command inside, or copy a file into or out of, a microVM that already exists. This is everyday use: the machine's network egress and shares were fixed when it was created (and are reviewed by the provisioning rule), and kindling only accepts exec/cp on machines started with -allow-exec or created as sandboxes. It is listed at medium so a user can turn it off independently of the stronger rules.
permissions.label: kindling guest command execution
safer_guidance: Run untrusted code in a throwaway `kling sandbox create` with the default -egress none rather than in a long-lived machine.

Freeze machines instead of removing them, and snapshot volumes or database copies before a restore or reset.
Have a person hand credentials to the credential proxy; the guest then only sees a placeholder.
